feedback.end: The woman with the clipboard represents organising things. This can help you cope with negative feelings.

instruction.text: Does this help you get organised? Decide quickly!

atoms.a: making a list of my homework
throwing loose papers into my bag
making a plan for the weekend
organising an activity with my friend
not writing down my homework for the day
planning how to do a craft
leaving my school work on the kitchen table

atoms.b: Sometimes, negative feelings occur because we feel ((++out_of_control in_control)). Organising things can help big tasks feel more manageable by ((++breaking_them_up_into_smaller_steps hoping_the_feelings_will_go_away)).

feedback.end: The lady reading represents shifting your attention. To avoid taking small things and thinking them into big problems, we can shift our attention away and do other fun things instead.

instruction.text: How could each child shift their attention away from their problem? Match the child to the strategy that would fit them best. You can learn more about the children and strategies by selecting the images and listening.

a.sound: Mark loves to read stories. He failed a test today and is feeling awful about it.
Jonathan enjoys thinking games. He and his best friend got in a fight today, and he can’t stop thinking about it.
Eileen loves crime dramas. She fought with her mum about music classes and doesn’t know what to do.
Jenny loves making new things. Her PE teacher yelled at her for not paying attention during rugby training, and she has felt bad ever since.

atoms.b: When shifting your attention, you should always choose activities that you ((++enjoy hate)). Personal coping strategies need to suit ((++you everyone_else)): that’s why they’re personal!
